items.label: text
items.text: Some naturally occurring aldehydesandketonesare important inliving systems. Somefunction assex hormones;others are used as flavourings.Forexample, testosterone,the malesex hormone,and progesterone, a hormonesecreted by the ovaries thatstimulates thegrowthofcellsinthe uterinewall,bothcontain a ketone functional group. Aldehydescanbefound in foods,perfumes and medicines.Some aldehydes areresponsibleforvery pleasanttastes and odours, suchasvanillinfromvanilla beans,benzaldehydefrom almondsandcinnamaldehyde from cinnamon.About 82%ofthechemicals present in coriander leaves arealdehydeswith9or 10 carbonatomsinthe molecules.

items.text: Wemet carbonyl compounds briefly inBook 1,but only as the products of the oxidation of alcohols.

items.label: text
items.text: types of compounds contain this group (such as carboxylic acids, which contain COOH), but only two types are classified as carbonyl compounds-these are aldehydes and ketones.

items.label: text
items.text: A carbonyl compound is described as an aldehyde if there is a hydrogen atom joined to the carbonyl group. The naming system uses the suffix -al, and the carbon chain is named in the same way as an alkane. If locants are used, then the carbon of the carbonyl group is carbon 1 in the chain. Table A shows some examples.

items.label: table
items.text:
| STRUCTURALFORMULA   | NAME                | COMMONNAME         |
|---------------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| HCHO                | methanal            | formaldehyde       |
| CH;CHO              | ethanal             | acetaldehyde       |
| CH;CH2CHO           | propanal            | (propionaldehyde)  |
| (CH3)CHCHO          | methylpropanal      | (isobutyraldehyde) |
| CH;CHCH2CHO         | butanal             | (butyraldehyde)    |
| CHsCHO              | benzenecarbaldehyde | benzaldehyde       |

items.label: text
items.text: A carbonyl compound is described as aketone if there are only hydrocarbon groups joined to the carbonyl group. The naming system uses the suffx-one,and the carbon chain is named in the same way as an alkane.If locants are used, then one of the end carbon atoms in the chain of the carbonyl group is carbon 1 in the chain. The rules about using the lowest possible numbers, as with alkanes, apply to ketones. Table B shows some examples.

items.label: table
items.text:
| STRUCTURALFORMULA   | NAME                | COMMONNAME                |
|---------------------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| CH;COCH3            | propanone           | acetone                   |
| CH;COCHCH3          | butanone            | (methyl ethyl ketone)     |
| CHCOCHCHCH3         | pentan-2-one        | (methyl propyl ketone)    |
| CH;CHCOCHCH3        | pentan-3-one        | (diethyl ketone)          |
| (CH3)2CHCOCH3       | 3-methylbutan-2-one | (methyl isopropyl ketone) |
